heros.infro: Sicily general and strategist. He have a wide range of knowledge.
heros.name: George of Antioch

heros.infro: Manuela Beltrán was a Colombian woman was unusual for her time in that she was literate and owned her own grocery business. She organized a peasant revolt against the harsh taxation of the Spanish Empire's colonies by reading the edict of the new taxation regimen in the main square of Socorro to the outrage of the crowd.
heros.name: Manuela Beltran

heros.infro: Ralpacan was the 41st King of Tibet. He's considered one of three "Dharma" Kings and is responsible for bringing Budhism to Tibet. Under his rule the Tibetan Empire reached its greatest extent including parts of Nepal, India, China, and other lands. He promoted the development of Tibetan literature and culture, standardized weights and measures, and built the magnificent multi-functional nine-storied temple of U-shang-rdo used for political, academic, and religious purposes.
heros.name: Ralpacan

heros.infro: Rani Rudrama Devi was one of the most prominent rulers of the Kakatiya Dynasty in India. She succeeded her father at age fourteen. She suppressed uprisings within the Kakatiya territory and incursions by neighboring kingdoms. One of her accomplishments was the construction of the Warangal Fort. She embraced an extinct form of dance known as Shiva Tandavam Perini as an exercise for the soldiers and made it an part of the royal force training.
heros.name: Rani Rudrama Devi

heros.infro: Amin al-Din Rashid was a 13th century Persian physician, who specialized as a dietician for the Persian court. He composed a large treatise on the proper preparation of food and drink, which was to be used by the servants of the rulers of Persia.
heros.name: Amin al-Din Rashid

heros.infro: Changamire ruled East Africa in the area of present-day Zimbabwe. He succeeded his father after slaying the rightful heir to the Mwene Mutapa clan. He then warred against the Rozvi Empire that held all of Zimbabwe and Mozambique and acquired the gold-rich central and southern provinces except for the coastal ports. Changamire's heirs ruled the Rozvi Kingdom until forced to recognize Portuguese invaders as overlords in 1629.
heros.name: Changamire

heros.infro: An advisor to Mary, Queen of Scots, Bothwell was a Scottish Protestant nobleman and hereditary Lord High Admiral of Scotland. When Mary's second husband, Lord Darnley, was murdered, Bothwell was tried and acquitted of the deed in 1567. In quick order, Mary named him Duke of Orkney and Shetland, Bothwell divorced his wife, and he and Mary were wed. When the English defeated Mary's army and took her prisoner, Bothwell fled Scotland to raise an army in Scandinavia but was imprisoned on suspicion of Darnley's murder. Bothwell died in a Danish prison.
heros.name: James Hepburn, Earl of Bothwell

heros.infro: Grandson of Anglo-Saxon King Edmund II, Edgar was heir to the throne of Edward the Confessor, but, in 1066, the Witan (council) chose Harold Godwin instead. Harold was killed in the Battle of Hastings against the Norman William the Conqueror. The Witan elected Edgar king of the Anglo-Saxons, but Edgar, unable to mount effective resistance against William, submitted to him and finally joined his court in 1074. Edgar commanded forces in the First Crusade and died in Scotland in 1126.
heros.name: Edgar the Etheling

heros.infro: Born of Arthurian royal blood lines, Agravain is an able bodied fighter and leader of men though most of his more memorial victories were won with cunning and deceit and not the sword.
heros.name: Sir Agravain

heros.infro: Apprenticed first to a goldsmith, Botticelli became a renowned painter in his native Florence. He created religious artwork, including some frescoes completed in 1480-82 in the Sistine Chapel in Rome, and was a gifted portraitist. His secular subjects were painted for cultured clients like Lorenzo de Medici and Duke Cosimo de Medici. His large painting of The Birth of Venus is among his most famous works.
heros.name: Sandro Botticelli 2

heros.infro: Cardinal Richelieu first was Secretary of State for France in 1616. In 1622 he became a cardinal and chief minister for Louis XIII . He is considered to be the world's first prime minister in the modern sense of the position.
heros.name: Cardinal Richelieu

heros.infro: Thaddeus Kosciuszko was a Polish-Lithuanian military leader. He fought in War for Independence with the rank of colonel in the Continental Army. Afterwards he led the 1794 Revolt against Russia and Prussia.
heros.name: Thaddeus Kosciuszko

heros.infro: Italian explorer, navigator and cartographer. He participated in several voyages that explored the coast of South America.
heros.name: Amerigo Vespucci

heros.infro: Eldest son of Louis the Pious, while in power as the Holy Roman Emperor he claimed the land his father had divided up between several parties prior to his death as his own.  His bold move was met with swift resistance and he was defeated easily by his brother Louis the German.  Although he failed, he retained some power after the peace negotiations.
heros.name: Lothair I

heros.infro: Aside from his passion for painting, Durer developed mathematic theories of proportions and perspective which were widely used in art.
heros.name: Albrecht Durer

heros.infro: Roman philosopher, statesman, lawyer, political theorist, and Roman constitutionalist. Cicero is widely considered one of Rome's greatest orators and prose stylists.
heros.name: Cicero

heros.infro: Li Shangyin, also known as Yishan, was a Chinese poet of the late Tang Dynasty who had a moderately successful career in the imperial civil service. He is known for the imagist quality of his work. His poetry is sensual and suggestive of political, biographical or philosophical insinuations, making translation very difficult.
heros.name: Li Shangyin

heros.infro: Spending his working life in Lunéville in the duchy of Lorraine, La Tour's career was disrupted by disastrous wars in the region. An original, individual style of religious paintings and genre works arose from this conflict. Largely forgotten after his death in 1652, La Tour's paintings enjoyed a rebirth in popularity in the 20th century.
heros.name: Georges de La Tour

heros.infro: A key figure in the English Civil War (1642-1649), Cromwell rose to leadership of the Parliamentarians (Roundheads). Also a brilliant general and military tactician, he organized the cavalry and the New Model Army. Resounding victories at Naseby and Preston won the war over the Royalists (Cavaliers). Cromwell ousted royal sympathizers from Parliament and signed the warrant for the execution of King Charles I. For the new Commonwealth of England, he repressed opposition in England, Scotland, and Ireland. In 1653, he dismissed Parliament becoming Lord Protector of the Commonwealth. Cromwell's Protectorate was a military regime that he spent the rest of his life trying to legitimize constitutionally.
heros.name: Oliver Cromwell
